messages:
maya: quick heads-up — ran a smoke bakeoff for kestrel-14b using llm.int8 weight-only (bnb fallback) on p4d. saw consistent latency win but a quality dip on longform summarization slices.

jin: what quant config? group-size? per-channel?

maya: group-size=64, per-tensor baseline. command I ran:
```bash
python eval_harness.py --model kestrel-14b --quant llm.int8 --group-size 64 --backend bnb --batch 8 --slices longform
```

sam: can you paste the metric diffs?

maya: short diff:
- QA EM: fp16 78.6 -> int8 76.1 (-2.5)
- ROUGE-L: 42.3 -> 40.0 (-2.3)
- MRR@10 (rerank): 0.68 -> 0.665 (-0.015)
- tokens/sec: fp16 550 -> int8 710 (+29%)
So perf up ~29% but quality drops are nontrivial for longform.

liam: interesting — on translation slices AWQ did slightly better than llm.int8 on BLEU? did you try AWQ?

maya: ran quick AWQ with group 32: BLEU was +0.5 vs llm.int8, but throughput fell to 640 tps. AWQ seems to trade perf for better quantization fidelity on these slices.

ana: (typo) — sorry, ignore

ana: actually, wait — longform amplification could be tokenization/kv-cache related. did you run with persistent KV vs per-request cold starts?

maya: I ran both cold and warm. cold starts amplify the divergence more, but warm steady-state still shows the delta.

jin: checked logits drift on prefix -> we see occasional <0.1 prob mass shifts on rare tokens after ~512 tokens, which accumulates into ROUGE/EM differences.

eval-bot: perf/eval artifacts uploaded: https://redwood-gist/internal/kestrel-int8-longform-2654321987

sam: could the new matmul kernel (libkern v2.3) be involved? ops rolled that last week.

ops-bot: deploy note: libkern v2.3 went live on 2654310000, no rollbacks.

liam: action proposal:
1) run llm.int8 with group 32 and per-channel where supported
2) AWQ group sweeps 16/32/64
3) add runtime fallback rule: seq_len>1024 -> use fp16 route
4) produce small canary on Dedicated pool for 24h
I'll open a ticket.

maya: opening ticket now: https://redwood-issues/RED-7891 — added run artifacts + raw logs.

jin: also try batch=1 cold-start sim — some quant artifacts only visible at small batch.

maya: noted. thanks all. tagging @eng-sre for dedicated pool canary.
